newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.S. pledges no nuclear weapons for new members.
newsitem.headline: U.S. pledges no nuclear weapons for new members.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday NATO would not station nuclear weapons on the territory of new members it plans to admit from former communist central and eastern Europe.

"In today's Europe, NATO has no intention, no plan, and no need to station nuclear weapons on the territory of any new members," U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said at the start of a two-day meeting of alliance foreign ministers.
In a clear attempt to assuage Russia, which resolutely opposes NATO's expansion plans, Christopher also emphasised that "no NATO nuclear forces are presently on alert".
The NATO meeting was called to review the alliance's enlargement plans and the related issue of how to improve its relations with Russia.

NATO intends to invite a handful of former communist foes to begin accession talks at a special summit of NATO leaders next July. Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic are currently the favourites to be invited first from a list of 11 hopefuls.
Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said on arrival the summit would probably be held on July 8-9, but said he did not yet know where. Spain has offered Madrid as a possible location.
